raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Muse Glimmer sometimes ends a tool call's last parameter without `</atem:parameter>`. The Python Muse tool parser drops that parameter, which leaves `{}` for a call with one parameter. The Rust parser rejects the whole ATEM block, and the Rust frontend then sends the raw markup to the client as text. Both parsers now end such a value where its `</atem:invoke>` begins.

## Claims

- Python (`MuseToolParser`): a last parameter missing `</atem:parameter>` keeps its value. Before this change it was dropped silently, and earlier closed parameters were kept.
- Rust (`MuseUnifiedParser`): the same input parses into the tool call. Before this change it failed with `invalid Muse ATEM block`, and `unified.rs` fell back to plain text.
- Output for well-formed calls is unchanged.
- The Muse section of `docs/features/tool_calling.md` states the rule.

## Validation

New tests, 4 per parser: an unclosed only parameter, an unclosed last parameter after a closed one, an unclosed parameter followed by a second invoke in the same block, and an unclosed string value followed by its separating newline.

Python, on the base commit (5118d990) with only the tests added:

```
$ pytest -q tests/tool_use/test_muse.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py
E       AssertionError: assert {} == {'chunk_ids':...9-389d-4601']}
E       AssertionError: assert {'query': 'foosball bracket'} == {'query': 'fo..., 'limit': 10}
E       AssertionError: assert [{}, {'query'...all bracket'}] == [{'chunk_ids'...all bracket'}]
E       AssertionError: assert {} == {'query': 'foosball bracket'}
4 failed, 97 passed
```

With the fix:

```
$ pytest -q tests/tool_use/test_muse.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py tests/tool_use/test_muse_parse_delta.py
101 passed, 17 skipped
```

Rust, before the fix:

```
$ cargo test -p vllm-parser --lib muse_unclosed
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Tool(ParsingFailed { message: "near \"<atem:function_calls>\\n<atem:invoke name=\\\"cite\\\">\\n<atem:parameter name=\\\"chunk_ids\\\"\": invalid Muse ATEM block" })
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 4 failed
```

The test with a second invoke also guards the boundary in `atem_parameter_value`: without the check that a closed value does not contain `</atem:invoke>`, the first invoke's value runs into the second invoke and the block yields 1 call instead of 2.

With the fix: `cargo test -p vllm-parser` passes 628 of 628, and `cargo test -p vllm-chat --test roundtrip` passes 25 of 25. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings`, ruff 0.14.0 and markdownlint are clean.

I also checked the regex against real model output, from `Inferact/Muse-Glimmer-30B-NVFP4-W4A4` served by `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.32.0` during a 500-question agentic RAG evaluation. In v0.32.0 the regex lives in `muse_glimmer_tool_parser.py`. For every response with tool calls, I requested `return_token_ids`, decoded the ids with the server's `/detokenize` (framing tokens kept), and parsed that text with the v0.32.0 parser and with the patched one. The same generated tokens go through both parsers, so the comparison is deterministic.

| | Responses with tool calls | Unpatched parser reproduces the served calls | Calls the patch recovers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 500 questions | 2,273 | 2,273 | 190 (161 `cite`, 23 `search`, 6 `execute_code`) |

All 190 recovered calls had arrived with `{}` arguments, and each one gained exactly its one missing parameter.

## Details

Root cause: `_PARAM_RE` required a closing `</atem:parameter>`. On text like

```
<atem:invoke name="cite">
<atem:parameter name="chunk_ids">["07657059-389d-4601"]</atem:invoke>
```

the regex finds no match for that parameter, so it is skipped. Here it is the call's only parameter, so the call reaches the client with `{}`. The Rust `atem_parameter` uses `take_until(PARAMETER_CLOSE)` followed by `literal(PARAMETER_CLOSE)`, so the invoke fails, and with it the block.

Fix: a value ends at the earlier of `</atem:parameter>` (consumed) and `</atem:invoke>` (left for the invoke). A value that ends at the invoke drops the newline before `</atem:invoke>`. The Python regex and the Rust `atem_parameter_value` implement the same rule. A value cannot cross its invoke in either parser.

Limitations:

- No `RemoteOpenAIServer` test. The trigger is sampled output from the 30B checkpoint, which I cannot reproduce deterministically in CI. The parser tests use the exact text the model produced.
- The Rust frontend was not run end to end with the model. Its fix is covered by the unit tests and the chat roundtrip suite.
- #62345 fixes a different problem, quadratic attribute scans, but edits the same `_PARAM_RE` line (`[^>]*?` to `[^<>]*?`). The two changes touch different parts of the pattern, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

files.patch:
@@ -601,6 +601,8 @@ The parsers route `to=self` and recipient-less messages to reasoning,
 `to=user` and `to=commentary` messages to content, and tool recipients to
 ATEM tool-call extraction. `to=developer` messages are omitted. Framing
 special tokens are preserved for parsing and removed from surfaced content.
+When a call's last parameter has no closing `</atem:parameter>`, its value
+ends at `</atem:invoke>`.
 
 The Rust frontend also provides a Muse unified parser under `muse` and
 `musespark1x`, and selects it automatically for Muse Spark model names.

@@ -173,6 +173,65 @@ def test_json_object_array_and_bool_params_decode():
     }
 
 
+def test_unclosed_last_parameter_ends_at_invoke_close():
+    """The model sometimes omits the final </atem:parameter>."""
+    raw = (
+        "<|start|>assistant to=cite<|message|>"
+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="cite">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="chunk_ids">["07657059-389d-4601"]</atem:invoke>\n'
+        "</atem:function_calls><|eot|>"
+    )
+    out = MuseToolParser.extract_tool_calls(T, raw, _NO_REQ)
+    assert out.tools_called and len(out.tool_calls) == 1
+    assert json.loads(out.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {
+        "chunk_ids": ["07657059-389d-4601"]
+    }
+
+
+def test_unclosed_last_parameter_after_closed_one():
+    raw = (
+        "<|start|>assistant to=search<|message|>"
+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="search">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="query">foosball bracket</atem:parameter>\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="limit">10\n'
+        "</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls><|eot|>"
+    )
+    out = MuseToolParser.extract_tool_calls(T, raw, _NO_REQ)
+    assert json.loads(out.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {
+        "query": "foosball bracket",
+        "limit": 10,
+    }
+
+
+def test_unclosed_last_parameter_stays_inside_its_invoke():
+    raw = (
+        "<|start|>assistant to=cite<|message|>"
+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="cite">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="chunk_ids">["07657059-389d-4601"]</atem:invoke>\n'
+        '<atem:invoke name="search">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="query">foosball bracket</atem:parameter>\n'
+        "</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls><|eot|>"
+    )
+    out = MuseToolParser.extract_tool_calls(T, raw, _NO_REQ)
+    assert [json.loads(c.function.arguments) for c in out.tool_calls] == [
+        {"chunk_ids": ["07657059-389d-4601"]},
+        {"query": "foosball bracket"},
+    ]
+
+
+def test_unclosed_last_string_parameter_drops_separator_newline():
+    raw = (
+        "<|start|>assistant to=search<|message|>"
+        '<atem:function_calls>\n<atem:invoke name="search">\n'
+        '<atem:parameter name="query">foosball bracket\n'
+        "</atem:invoke>\n</atem:function_calls><|eot|>"
+    )
+    out = MuseToolParser.extract_tool_calls(T, raw, _NO_REQ)
+    assert json.loads(out.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {
+        "query": "foosball bracket"
+    }
+
+
 # ------------------------------------------------- reasoning -> tool handoff

@@ -89,11 +89,14 @@
 # "<|start|>assistant", so the model's first emitted text is " to=self<|message|>").
 _OPEN_TAIL_TO_RE = re.compile(r"[^\S\n]+to=[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*$")
 
-# --- Tool-call extraction (unchanged from MUSE_GLIMMER_RESPONSE_SCHEMA) -------------
+# --- Tool-call extraction ---------------------------------------------------
 _INVOKE_RE = re.compile(r"(<atem:invoke\b.*?</atem:invoke>)", re.DOTALL)
 _NAME_RE = re.compile(r'<atem:invoke\b[^>]*?\bname="([^"]+)"')
+# The model sometimes omits the last </atem:parameter>, so a value also ends
+# where its invoke closes.
 _PARAM_RE = re.compile(
-    r'<atem:parameter\b[^>]*?\bname="(?P<key>[^"]+)"[^>]*?>(?P<value>.*?)</atem:parameter>',
+    r'<atem:parameter\b[^>]*?\bname="(?P<key>[^"]+)"[^>]*?>(?P<value>.*?)'
+    r"(?:</atem:parameter>|\n?(?=</atem:invoke>))",
     re.DOTALL,
 )
 _FUNCTION_CALLS_OPEN = "<atem:function_calls>"
